headline: Southborough boards prepped for the March 2 school Special Town Meeting, approved water rate increases, and advanced municipal and regional school budgets.
synopsis: Town and school committees finalized positions ahead of the March 2 Special Town Meeting regarding Neary School renovation studies, alternative campus configurations, and roof replacement borrowing. The Select Board approved a 9 percent water rate increase and a 12.6 percent base charge hike for FY27 while weighing townwide staffing levels against a projected 6.4 percent tax levy rise. Meanwhile, the Regional School Committee adopted a $31.4 million operating budget, applying $675,000 in reserves to moderate Southborough's assessment increase to 4.83 percent. Additionally, the Planning Board voted to withdraw a proposed 55-plus housing bylaw from the Annual Town Meeting warrant following resident feedback.

highlights.title: Town boards finalize recommendations for March 2 school warrant articles
highlights.why: School officials and the Select Board endorsed Article 1 for a $175,000 Neary renovation study and Article 4 for roof borrowing, while opposing Articles 2 and 3 to study closing Neary. If Article 1 passes, the Article 4 roof borrowing request will be reduced from $6.85 million to $4.5 million.

highlights.title: Select Board approves FY27 water rate and base charge increases
highlights.why: The board voted unanimously to raise volumetric rates by 9.0 percent and base charges by 12.6 percent to fund capital projects and rebuild reserves. The change will increase the average quarterly residential bill by about $16.

highlights.title: Regional School Committee approves $31.4 million FY27 budget
highlights.why: Driven by special education and insurance increases, the committee passed an operating budget that applies $675,000 from reserves, bringing Southborough's operating assessment increase to 4.83 percent.

highlights.title: Select Board reviews FY27 operating budget and police staffing
highlights.why: Facing a projected 6.4 percent tax levy increase and revenue deficit, the board debated whether to preserve two newly added police patrol positions or implement a hiring freeze to reduce costs.

highlights.title: Planning Board withdraws 55-plus housing bylaw from warrant
highlights.why: Following resident concerns regarding density, housing diversity, and alternative zoning approaches, the board voted 5-0 to pull the proposed bylaw from the Annual Town Meeting warrant for further study.

highlights.title: Regional School Committee adopts 2026-2027 calendar Option 5
highlights.why: The committee voted 4-1-1 to adopt calendar Option 5, scheduling the first day of school for September 1, 2026, and placing a staff professional development day on Orthodox Good Friday while removing them from Yom Kippur and Eid.

looking_ahead.what: Special Town Meeting on school feasibility studies and Neary roof borrowing at Trottier Middle School
looking_ahead.when: March 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM check-in, 6:00 PM meeting
